SMTO-UI-0060 — Account access changed

GUID: 47a24912-b8f2-5f30-aeb6-0dc54d96d546
Slug: account-changed
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • This page was opened for one SMTO account, but your browser is now signed in as a different account, often from another tab. SMTO refused this request so that one account's work doesn't land in another account's workspace.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy any text you typed but haven't sent yet. Reloading the page or signing out can clear unsent text.
  2. Check which account is signed in: your username appears next to the notification bell at the top of the page. Signing in as someone else in any tab switches every tab in this browser to that account.
  3. If it's the wrong account, select your username, choose Sign out, and sign in with the right one. If it's the right account, just reload the page. After this, the page and your sign-in belong to the same account, so SMTO accepts its requests.
  4. Before repeating your last action, check whether it already appears in the right workspace. This request was refused, but actions you took before the accounts switched may already have been saved.

What success looks like

  • The page loads under the account you expect and your own conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • If the message keeps coming back after reloading, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. To use two accounts at once, use a separate browser or a private window for the second one. Never include passwords or browser cookies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The portal middleware returned account_changed (401) because the account this page expects (X-SMTO-Account-Expectation header or smto_account query parameter) differs from the account of the browser's current session.

What this means

  • Your session no longer matches the current account permissions. This reports access to the current request, not the outcome of previous operations.

Why this can happen

  • Your session no longer matches the current account permissions.

How to diagnose it

  • The refreshed session shows the current account permissions.

How to fix it

  • Session cookies are shared by every tab, so signing in as another user anywhere in this browser invalidates pages opened under the previous account. Reload the page so it starts with the current session's account, or sign out and sign in as the intended account; then check the intended workspace before repeating the refused action.
  • Sign in again to load current access. If a needed feature is still unavailable, ask an administrator to review your access.

Retry and execution caution

  • The refreshed session shows the current account permissions.

How to verify the fix

  • The refreshed session shows the current account permissions.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
